title: Persisted column layouts and adaptive sparse density profiles for virtual tables
creator: Ava Martínez
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table currently supports column resizing and density modes, but users lose fine-grained adjustments when they navigate away or switch projects. Engineering has also raised concerns about state size and rehydration costs when persisting per-user layouts.

Goal: Design a compact, robust UX for persisting column widths, order, and density preferences across sessions while keeping on-disk/state payloads small and compatible with server-side account storage. Introduce 'sparse density profiles' — a way for users to pick a general density preset (Comfortable / Compact / Sparse) and then optionally tune a small set of per-column density overrides (e.g., row-height multiplier or compactness toggles) that are persisted.

Key user stories:
- As a power user I want my column width and order preserved per workspace so I don't reconfigure my dashboard after each login.
- As a new user I want sane defaults that match my display size and device density.
- As an accessibility-first user I need keyboard-first column resizing and clear focus affordances preserved.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Persistence storage must be small: limit per-layout payload to ~1KB. We will store deltas from the default layout (sparse diff) instead of full serialized column objects.
- Virtualization compatibility: KV cache and virtualization indexing must tolerate small width changes without re-creating the entire viewport. We will handshake with engineering to implement debounced resize events and CSS transforms rather than forcing full reflow.
- Backend vs client storage: default to client (localStorage) for anonymous/self-serve users; provide optional account-backed storage for logged-in users via a compact API (POST /api/v1/layouts). This enables cross-device sync but requires migration and opt-in consent UI.
- Performance: avoid storing pixel-perfect values; instead store normalized widths (0-1) with min/max enforcement.

Acceptance criteria:
- Users can save and restore column width/order and density profile per workspace.
- Default table load remains < 10ms additional parse time for persisted data on modern browsers.
- Keyboard resize flow exists and is discoverable via tooltip and a11y docs; ARIA roles and live regions included.
- Sparse density profile UI: users can choose a preset, open an optional panel to tweak per-column compactness, and see live preview.
- Designs delivered to engineering include edge states (RTL, pinned columns, hidden columns), and a migration plan for legacy persisted layouts.

Deliverables:
- Figma frames: global settings panel, per-table layout menu, compactness tweak panel, tooltip microcopy, keyboard-resize modal.
- Prototype (code sandbox) showing debounced resize + virtualization-safe reflow.
- PRD with storage schema and API contract for persisted layouts.

Open questions for engineering:
- What is our canonical place to store small per-user preferences server-side (existing user-settings service or new layouts endpoint)?
- Should persistence be enabled by default for logged-in users or require explicit opt-in? Recommendation: enabled with easy revert and one-click clear layout.

Notes on accessibility:
- Keyboard resize: arrow keys to nudge, modifier to accelerate, ESC to cancel, Enter to commit. Provide short inline help the first time a user focuses a column edge.
- Live region announces new column width and density changes.

References:
- Internal PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UX/pages/PROJ-Table+Persistence+PRD
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Table-Layouts-2026
comments: 2026-01-12 - Kickoff: synced with Eng (Samir Kapoor) and PM (Nora Patel). Agreement to use sparse diffs to minimize payload. Action: design to spec delta schema.
2026-01-20 - Early explorations: created three density presets and two variants for per-column overrides. Usability note: users liked a compact toggle in the column header for quick tweaks.
2026-01-28 - Engineering review: Liam asked for normalized widths instead of raw pixels to simplify responsive breakpoints. Updated designs accordingly.
2026-02-03 - Accessibility review: added ARIA live region text and keyboard acceleration modifier. Daniel (a11y) asked for a first-time helper overlay; added as optional onboarding step.
2026-02-10 - Prototype: interactive sandbox linked in attachments. Dev feedback: virtualization recompute spike when toggling density; agreed on 120ms debounce and incremental row-height updates.
2026-02-18 - User testing (5 participants): power users appreciated persistence; some confusion around 'sparse density' term — changed copy to 'Density profile with column overrides'.
2026-02-24 - Design review: PM approved acceptance criteria. Engineering asked to add explicit clear/reset control in the UI. Added ‘Reset layout’ and confirm modal.
2026-02-28 - Hand-off: Figma finalized and assets uploaded. Opening frontend PR to implement initial client-side persistence.
